summary: Based on what you've told me (no children, all in their thirties, household earnings of $300,000 to $500,000 a year), none of the ten programmes look like a fit. SNAP, WIC, TANF, SSI, Medicaid, CHIP, the EITC, the refundable child tax credit, ACA premium tax credits, and free or reduced-price school meals all have income limits far below your household's earnings, and the child-based programmes don't apply without children. This holds in any state. I didn't ask about your state or other details because your income is well above every limit, so they wouldn't change the result. If your household income is actually much lower than you described, please tell me and I'll rescreen.
